units.function: move from a threat to the question of how to measure it

original_instantiations: a state that cannot meet demand is called vulnerable, so the measuring question follows at once
the threat sentence hands straight off to the measurement problem

units.source_excerpt: A fragile state cannot meet its people's demands. As a result, how to measure the fragility of countries counts.
units.reusable_pattern: let the threat sentence end on the verb counts
prohibited_generalizations: do not open on the method

units.function: list the methods in the order they are applied

original_instantiations: one method takes the latest value, another averages with a decaying weight, and the decay is then justified
each method gets its own clause and its own reason

units.source_excerpt: We apply the latest-determine method and the weighted average method. Moreover, we use the exponential weighting pattern to have realistic time-relating weights.
units.reusable_pattern: stack the methods and attach a reason to the last one
prohibited_generalizations: do not list methods without a reason

units.function: divide one effect into two named parts

original_instantiations: climate damage is split into a general part and an extreme part before either is defined
the names come before the definitions

units.source_excerpt: We divide effects of climate change into two parts: general impacts and extreme impacts.
units.reusable_pattern: name both halves before defining either
prohibited_generalizations: do not define before the split

units.function: claim the model works at both ends of the scale

original_instantiations: a reweighting is introduced so the model can be said to work for both smaller and larger states
the result is stated as a finding, not a hope

units.source_excerpt: In order to make our model more applicable, we use a re-weighting method. In this way, we find the model works well in smaller or larger states.
units.reusable_pattern: state a modification and then the finding it buys
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim generality without the modification

units.function: open on a small scene before the claim

original_instantiations: a winter scene of coats coming off on a flight comes before the claim that climate shapes how people live
the scene does the work of a definition

units.source_excerpt: It is always an interesting experience in winter seeing passengers taking off their sweaters on the plane flying from north to south.
units.reusable_pattern: open a technical section with one concrete scene
prohibited_generalizations: do not open every section with a definition

units.function: rename a concept by its opposite in the same sentence

original_instantiations: stability is named and then immediately restated as its opposite, fragility
the aside does the redefining

units.source_excerpt: Nowadays it significantly impacts the stability, or saying conversely, the fragility of a country.
units.reusable_pattern: restate a term by its opposite inside the sentence
prohibited_generalizations: do not correct the term in a later sentence

units.function: warn that the indicators feed each other

original_instantiations: fragility and social conditions are said to reinforce each other once any one index turns severe
the warning justifies measuring more than one thing

units.source_excerpt: A state's fragility interplays with its social conditions and they can easily fall into a cycle once one of the indexes becomes severe.
units.reusable_pattern: warn that one bad index pulls the others down
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat the indicators as independent

units.function: mark a claim about other work as the authors' own assumption

original_instantiations: the word almost is kept so the authors can say they are guessing the other lists' weights
the hedge is explained rather than left standing

units.source_excerpt: Here we use almost to assume their weighting systems, considering climate to have minor impacts on fragility.
units.reusable_pattern: explain the hedge word instead of deleting it
prohibited_generalizations: do not cite other work's weights as fact

units.function: assign each section a job

original_instantiations: the assumptions, the indicator calculations and the analysis are each pinned to a section number
the roadmap skips the sections it has nothing to say about

units.source_excerpt: In one section we state the basic assumptions. In the next we give a detailed explanation for each indicator.
units.reusable_pattern: preview only the sections that carry a job
reusable_elements: a verb of what happens there
prohibited_generalizations: do not preview every section

units.function: state an assumption as a flat numbered sentence

original_instantiations: each assumption is one numbered sentence with no defence attached
the defence is left for later

units.source_excerpt: States can exchange resources and communicate with neighbouring states.
units.reusable_pattern: give each assumption its own numbered line and nothing more
prohibited_generalizations: do not defend an assumption in the list

units.function: narrow an assumption with one stressed case

original_instantiations: resources are said to move quickly, and the disaster case is singled out
the stressed case does the justifying

units.source_excerpt: Within a country, resources can be dispatched quickly from rich places to poor areas, especial when some parts are suffering catastrophe.
units.reusable_pattern: keep the general claim and bolt one case onto it
prohibited_generalizations: do not smooth the paper's grammar

units.function: explain a name as the initials it was built from

original_instantiations: the model's name is unpacked into the four words whose first letters make it
the unpacking doubles as the list of fields

units.source_excerpt: The name for our model is the combination of the four first letters of security, politics, economics and climate.
units.reusable_pattern: let the acronym introduce the four fields
prohibited_generalizations: do not leave an acronym unexplained

units.function: promise to take the fields one at a time

original_instantiations: the factors are sorted into four fields and then promised one field at a time
the manner phrase sets the pace of the section

units.source_excerpt: We classify the factors into four main fields. We introduce the quantification field-by-field.
units.reusable_pattern: announce the order of treatment as field by field
prohibited_generalizations: do not mix the fields in one paragraph

units.function: define an indicator as one of two scores

original_instantiations: a country scores nothing if a coup happened in fifteen years and full marks otherwise
the rule is stated as two cases and nothing between

units.source_excerpt: A country scores nothing if there have been any coups in the last fifteen years and scores full marks if else.
units.reusable_pattern: score an indicator with two cases and no middle
prohibited_generalizations: do not add a middle value the paper lacks

units.function: say the indicators were chosen to count equally

original_instantiations: the four indicators are defined so that each reflects the state to the same degree, and smaller factors are dropped
the equal grading is a decision, not a result

units.source_excerpt: We define the four indicators to reflect the political appearance of a state to the same large extent and ignore other minor factors.
units.reusable_pattern: declare equal weight by how the indicators were defined
reusable_elements: a to the same extent phrase
prohibited_generalizations: do not hide an equal weighting inside the formula

units.function: sort indicators by how long their effect lasts

original_instantiations: some indicators hit suddenly and others keep working, so each kind gets its own method
the count of each kind is given

units.source_excerpt: Some indicators have an abrupt and sudden impact, while others have an on-going influence.
units.reusable_pattern: split the indicators by the length of their effect
prohibited_generalizations: do not use one method for both kinds

units.function: defend a chosen constant as reasonable

features.quantitative_role: a decay of fifteen percent a year
original_instantiations: the constant could be anything in the range, yet one value is called reasonable for the fading it describes
the concession comes before the verdict

units.source_excerpt: Though the constant can be an arbitrary constant in the range, the value chosen is rational to quantify the impact variation with time goes by.
units.reusable_pattern: admit the constant is free and then defend one value
prohibited_generalizations: do not present a free constant as derived

units.function: give a different time span a different reason

original_instantiations: a long span is given to conflicts because recovery is slow, and a short span to rights abuse because policy can change it
each span gets its own because

units.source_excerpt: A country suffering social conflicts needs a relatively longer time to recover. We assign a shorter span to rights abuse since it can be easily changed by policy.
units.reusable_pattern: match each window length to a reason
reusable_elements: a needs a longer time clause
prohibited_generalizations: do not set a window without saying why

units.function: read a formula by the direction it moves

original_instantiations: more people living low means a smaller indicator, which means a more fragile country
the chain runs from input to score to verdict

units.source_excerpt: More population living in low areas, smaller the value of the indicator is, and more fragile the country is.
units.reusable_pattern: gloss a formula as a chain of comparatives
prohibited_generalizations: do not repair the missing verbs

units.function: open a section by closing off disagreement

original_instantiations: doubt about the changing climate is dismissed before the consequence for states is drawn
the dismissal is the opener

units.source_excerpt: There is little doubt that the climate is changing and weather is becoming more extreme.
units.reusable_pattern: begin by saying the doubt is already settled
reusable_elements: a there is little doubt frame
prohibited_generalizations: do not reopen a premise the section treats as settled

units.function: justify one term as unavoidable

original_instantiations: worsening extremes make a term for rising emissions necessary in the formula
the necessity is stated, not derived

units.source_excerpt: Therefore a proportional item for emissions is of necessity in the formula to indicate the increasing difficulty of relief.
units.reusable_pattern: call a term necessary and then say what it stands for
prohibited_generalizations: do not add a term without saying it is needed

units.function: state both directions of a score

features.quantitative_role: a higher score against a lower one
original_instantiations: a higher score is read as less fragile and a lower score as more fragile
both directions are given so the reader cannot flip the scale

units.source_excerpt: Higher scores show less fragility while lower scores show more fragility.
units.reusable_pattern: give both ends of the scale in one sentence
prohibited_generalizations: do not leave the direction of a score implicit

units.function: single out the one term that pulls the other way

original_instantiations: only the extreme weather term is put underneath, and the sentence says what that does to the score
the placement and the effect are one sentence

units.source_excerpt: We only put the extreme weather indicator in the denominator, showing the negative correlation with the score.
units.reusable_pattern: mark the single term that works against the rest
prohibited_generalizations: do not let a negative term sit unexplained

units.function: cut a score into named bands

original_instantiations: the score is cut into fragile, vulnerable and stable, each with its own range
the bands are stated in rising order

units.source_excerpt: A score up to 27 is fragile, up to 50 is vulnerable, and up to 70 is stable.
units.reusable_pattern: name each band in the same sentence shape
prohibited_generalizations: do not leave the cut points to a table alone

units.function: read a number by which side of a threshold it falls on

original_instantiations: the country's extreme score is placed above the stated threshold and the meaning is given at once
the reading follows the comparison, not the number

units.source_excerpt: The direct climate indicator is larger than the threshold, which means the fragility is greatly influenced by extreme climate events.
units.reusable_pattern: compare with the threshold before interpreting
prohibited_generalizations: do not interpret a number without its threshold

units.function: give advice as a bare imperative

original_instantiations: the recommendations are given as bare commands with no subject and no hedging
the list form is the argument

units.source_excerpt: Improve political conditions and stop coups. Improve security conditions by stopping social conflicts.
units.reusable_pattern: let the advice stand as a bare command
prohibited_generalizations: do not pad advice with we suggest

units.function: praise a plotted relation in plain words

original_instantiations: the plotted relation is called beautiful and then said to confirm the earlier assumption
the praise comes before the use

units.source_excerpt: We find that the index and the self-regulatory factor have a beautiful linear relation. This relation confirms our assumption.
units.reusable_pattern: name the shape of a relation and then what it confirms
prohibited_generalizations: do not flatten a reaction to the plot

units.function: define a point as the moment a value is crossed

original_instantiations: the tipping point is defined as the moment the resistance falls to a stated value and keeps falling
the definition is a time, not a number

units.source_excerpt: The tipping point of a country is the time when its self-regulatory factor decreases to reach a set value and becomes lower.
units.reusable_pattern: define a threshold as a moment rather than a level
prohibited_generalizations: do not define a tipping point as a static number

units.function: close a definition by calling it reasonable

original_instantiations: countries under the line turn out to be the fragile ones, so the definition is called quite reasonable
the verdict is the authors' own

units.source_excerpt: Such countries with a small self-regulatory factor mostly are fragile. This shows our definition is quite reasonable.
units.reusable_pattern: let the evidence sentence end on quite reasonable
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim a definition is proven

units.function: warn with a condition and a consequence

original_instantiations: failing to fix one abuse is said to bring conflicts, which then pull the resistance down toward the line
the chain has three links

units.source_excerpt: If the country does not take effective measures, it may face more conflicts. This adverse trend will bring down the self-regulatory factor.
units.reusable_pattern: chain a failure to the line it crosses
prohibited_generalizations: do not skip the middle link

units.function: tie a proposal to the indicators it answers

original_instantiations: the eight proposals are said to be built in line with the climate indicators already defined
the link is asserted in one clause

units.source_excerpt: Our eight proposed interventions are in appliance with the climate indicators in the index.
units.reusable_pattern: anchor a proposal list to the indicators it serves
prohibited_generalizations: do not repair the preposition

units.function: admit the estimate is hard before giving it

original_instantiations: the prediction is called quite difficult, and only then is the method of estimating given
the admission earns the rough numbers

units.source_excerpt: It is quite difficult to accurately predict the expenses these measures required.
units.reusable_pattern: concede the difficulty before the estimate
reusable_elements: an it is quite difficult frame
prohibited_generalizations: do not present a rough estimate as exact

units.function: flag the thing the rescaling must not forget

original_instantiations: the change in area is said to be never the only change, and the affected fields are listed
the warning comes as a what's noteworthy sentence

units.source_excerpt: What is noteworthy is that it is never merely the change in land area; indicators in three fields are all affected.
units.reusable_pattern: warn that one change drags others with it
prohibited_generalizations: do not rescale one input and leave the rest

units.function: justify a weighting by who carries the burden

original_instantiations: countries high on the list are said to carry more responsibility, which is why the average is weighted
the weighting is argued, not assumed

units.source_excerpt: Countries that rank high have a high likelihood of instability. Therefore we determine the fragility by a weighted average.
units.reusable_pattern: derive the weighting from who bears the burden
prohibited_generalizations: do not weight without a reason

units.function: refuse to fill gaps and give the reason

original_instantiations: the gaps are left empty, and the reason is that filling them would invent a country's performance
the refusal is stated before the danger

units.source_excerpt: We do not fill these data gaps with imputed estimates. Our rationale is that the score is not significantly affected.
units.reusable_pattern: refuse an imputation and then give the rationale
prohibited_generalizations: do not impute missing data quietly

units.function: read robustness off curves that share a shape

original_instantiations: every curve for a different constant shows the same trend, so the model is called insensitive to it
the verdict names the constant

units.source_excerpt: Every curve representing a certain value shows the same trend. Therefore the model is not sensitive to the value of the constant.
units.reusable_pattern: call a model insensitive when the curves share a shape
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim robustness without the plot

units.function: claim many indicators protect against one wild one

original_instantiations: using many indicators across four fields is said to stop any single one from jerking the result
the protection is the point of the count

units.source_excerpt: We employ many indicators of four fields. In this way the model avoids the abrupt influence of a single indicator.
units.reusable_pattern: justify a long indicator list by what it prevents
reusable_elements: an avoids the abrupt influence phrase
prohibited_generalizations: do not add indicators without saying why

units.function: admit a dropped indicator and its cost

original_instantiations: an indicator is dropped for lack of data, and the possible error is named
the cost is a large error for some countries

units.source_excerpt: We neglect some indicators because we lack the accurate database, which may result in large fragility errors for some countries.
units.reusable_pattern: name the omitted indicator and the error it risks
prohibited_generalizations: do not hide a missing indicator

units.function: close by matching the result to a known list

original_instantiations: the computed scores are said to line up with an existing fragility list
the match is the credibility claim

units.source_excerpt: Our final score corresponds to the existing fragility index.
units.reusable_pattern: end on agreement with a published list
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim agreement without naming the list

units.function: list each source on its own numbered line

original_instantiations: the sources run from an encyclopedia entry to a journal article to a cited index
each entry keeps its own number

units.source_excerpt: References are numbered from an encyclopedia entry through a journal article to a cited index.
units.reusable_pattern: keep one source to a numbered line
prohibited_generalizations: do not merge two sources on one line

units.function: let the code stand for the method

original_instantiations: the hierarchy process is given as code that computes a consistency ratio and a weight vector
the listing is the derivation

units.source_excerpt: The appendix gives the hierarchy process as code that returns a consistency ratio and a weight vector.
units.reusable_pattern: put the derivation in code rather than in prose
prohibited_generalizations: do not describe code that is printed in full
